items.excerpt: Anadolu’s recap of top stories from around the globe Merve Aydogan 07 November 2026• Update: 07 November 2026 HAMILTON, Canada Here's a rundown of all the news you need to know for Saturday, including Russian President Vladimir Putin confirming that the next round of Russia-US-Ukraine talks will begin Tuesday in Abu Dhabi; US President Donald Trump naming Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff to replace Susie Wiles and saying he plans Cabinet changes after the midterm election losses; and bomb threats targeting flights, airports and media outlets in at least five European countries. Russian President Vladimir Putin confirmed that the next round of talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine is expected to begin next Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, with Russian state media reporting the talks would last two days. Putin said he invited members of the Russian delegation, headed by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, to a UN Security Council meeting ahead of the negotiations, Tass reported. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff previously said the parties intend to discuss security guarantees, de-escalation, humanitarian issues and further steps toward a peaceful settlement. - Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff, says he plans Cabinet changes after midterm losses Trump announced that Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff starting Monday, while Wiles moves to the Trump political operation. “Sometimes in life, you have to make moves,” Trump told reporters, saying he “wanted to make a change.” Trump said he plans to make changes to his Cabinet after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections earlier this week, telling CBS News’ 60 Minutes, “I do, yeah. Little bit,” when asked whether he plans to fire anyone, in an interview set to air Sunday. - Bomb threats target flights, media outlets in at least 5 European countries Bomb threats targeted flights, airports and media organizations in at least five European countries, prompting security inspections and evacuations, according to authorities and the media. Two aircraft departing from London and Brussels were diverted to Sofia and landed safely, while Czech police inspected nine aircraft following anonymous threats against four arrivals and five departures at Prague Airport. The French prime minister’s office said four aircraft flying over French territory received threats and all landed safely, and Copenhagen Police completed security checks at the city’s airport. Several Irish media organizations, including RTE, evacuated their premises after a threatening email was sent to broadcasters and news outlets in Ireland and Britain, with Irish Taoiseach Micheal Martin calling the threats “worrying.” The incidents followed similar threats Thursday against at least 18 flights across Europe.

items.title: Daly Says Fed May Need More Rate Increases as Inflation Persists | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: By Miriam Hart Nov 7, 2026, 9:43 AM UTC Updated Nov 7, 2026, 9:43 AM UTC 2 min read ... U.S. wage growth remained below the latest annual inflation reading, and San Francisco Federal Reserve Bank President Mary Daly said the Fed may need to raise rates again as price pressures persist. Daly made the assessment in a Nov. 6 interview with CNBC. She said officials would consider incoming economic information before deciding whether or when to act. “My expectation is we’re going to have to tighten policy further,” she said. Daly did not set a timetable or specify the size of a possible increase. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that employers added 165,000 jobs in October and unemployment edged down to 4.1%. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year earlier that month, while the consumer price index increased 3.7% year over year in September. Daly welcomed the job gains but said inflation continued to weigh on household finances. She said people were still finding work and spending, while pay gains failed to keep pace with prices. She described labor conditions as steady but not unusually strong, and said inflation’s persistence concerned her more than economic growth. Daly also said inflation had remained high for almost six years, with its burden spreading across households. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) raised its target range for the federal funds rate by 0.25 percentage point in September, to 3.75% to 4%. On Oct. 28, it left the range unchanged and said additional information would guide its policy stance. Daly said she supported both decisions and continued to favor a gradual approach. Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin also expects further increases may be needed, CNBC reported, though he has not identified when. The next report on October CPI is scheduled for Nov. 10, and the FOMC’s next meeting is set for Dec. 8-9.

items.excerpt: Published November 7, 2026 Updated November 7, 2026 07:01am By Reuters NEW YORK: The US dollar index jumped on Friday and was on pace for its biggest daily percentage gain in seven weeks as it extended gains after a stronger-than-expected US payrolls report. The Labor Department said US nonfarm payrolls jumped by 165,000 jobs last month, topping the 65,000 estimate of economists polled by Reuters, after an upwardly revised 60,000 gain in September, while the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1 percent. The report gives the Federal Reserve latitude to continue to hike interest rates, and market expectations for an increase of at least 25 basis points at the central bank’s December meeting moved back up towards 80 percent in the wake of the report, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. ... items.title: Americans feel a little better, and expect less inflation | How the World Works
items.excerpt: How the World Works · 7 Nov 2026 Key takeaways ... - Long-run expectations, at 3.4%, are still well above the Fed's 2% target, so one good month is not enough. ... ## What happened The University of Michigan's index of US consumer sentiment rose to 51.0 in its preliminary November reading, published on 6 November, from 48.0 in October. Economists had expected no change. Both parts of the index improved: views of current conditions rose to 51.0 from 46.7, and expectations to 50.9 from 48.8. Sentiment is still about 10% below its level in February, before the oil shock. The inflation households expect also eased. Over the next year, they expect prices to rise 4.3%, down from 4.7% in October and the lowest since August. Over the long run, five to ten years ahead, they expect 3.4%, down from 3.5%. In February, year-ahead expectations were 3.4%. ## Why expectations matter Inflation is partly self-fulfilling. If workers expect prices to rise 4% next year, they ask for bigger pay rises; if firms expect their costs to rise, they raise prices sooner. Both make the expected inflation more likely to happen. That is why central banks watch surveys like this one closely, especially the long-run measure: a rise there would suggest people have stopped believing inflation will return to target. Two weeks ago, these expectations were at a five-month high (our story). The fall in oil prices may have helped: fuel is the price households see most often, and it shapes what they expect. ## What it means for the Fed For the Federal Reserve, it is a mixed week. October's jobs report was strong, with 165,000 new jobs, which argues for a rate rise in December. Easing inflation expectations argue for patience. Long-run expectations of 3.4% are still well above the 2% target, and above the 2.8% to 3.2% range seen in 2024.

items.excerpt: - AP - Nov 7, 2026 - 7 hrs ago Russell Brand's convictions renew spotlight on media — and a culture — that may have looked away LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand's convictions this week for rape and sexual assault have renewed scrutiny on the BBC and other media employers that may have looked the other way. Brand, who gained fame while cultivating an outrageous persona, was convicted Thursday on multiple charges involving several women. The BBC has apologized for a culture that allowed his behavior to go unchecked. An internal probe followed a joint investigation by The Times and Channel 4, which aired accusations from women who said they were abused by Brand. Analysts argue that Brand's raunchy image acted as a shield, allowing his excesses to be overlooked by employers and the public, too. Writer Nick Harkaway expands his father John le Carré's spyverse in new thriller 'The Taper Man' LONDON (AP) — Fictional spymaster George Smiley is back in "The Taper Man," a new thriller set in the world of John le Carré and written by his son, Nick Harkaway. The novel follows Smiley to the U.S. in 1965, chasing a Soviet agent. Harkaway says writing a Cold War story in 2026 feels like “writing in the mirror” due to modern parallels. The book, published Nov. 17 in the U.S., is Harkaway’s second le Carré novel since his father’s death in 2020. Harkaway, who grew up with his father's stories, captures the le Carré spirit, blending espionage with office politics. He plans to write at least one more Smiley book and says other writers may be invited to expand the universe. Meghan's estranged father arrested and charged with possessing child sexual abuse materials TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old father of Prince Harry’s wife Meghan, has been arrested by federal agents in Florida and charged with possessing child sexual abuse material in California. Thomas Markle was released after a court appearance in Tampa. Authorities say a search of storage units in the Los Angeles area turned up dozens of items. There was no immediate comment from his lawyer. Meghan Markle had recently said she's “deeply distressed” about allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images were found at her father’s former home in the Philippines. 25 years after 'Britney,' 5 new Britney Spears songs showcase a pop icon at a transformative moment NEW YORK (AP) — Britney Spears' 2001 self-titled album ‘Britney' marked a pivotal moment in her career. At 19, she was already a global icon, transitioning from teen pop to a more mature sound. The album, certified quadruple platinum, showcased her evolution with hits like “I'm a Slave 4 U.” On Friday, Legacy Recordings releases the “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition).” It features five previously unreleased tracks and two new remixes. These songs add depth to her legacy, reflecting themes of autonomy and self-definition. Fans can revisit the album, exploring its impact and Spears’ journey from adolescence to adulthood. Awkwafina digs into her culinary roots to try something a little crazy: Open a restaurant NEW YORK (AP) — Awkwafina has taken a surprising turn in her career by diving into the culinary world. Her new Apple TV series, “Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook,” follows her journey from a novice cook to opening her own restaurant. The show, premiering Friday, captures her learning experiences, from making stir-fry to mastering Peking duck. Awkwafina was born Nora Lum and comes from a family with a rich restaurant history. They opened the New York City eatery Lum's. Her journey reconnects her with her roots and honors her family. The series also highlights a trend of Asian Americans returning to the restaurant industry, defying their parents' expectations. In 'Being Heumann,' Siân Heder and Ruth Madeley channel the spirit of a disability rights pioneer NEW YORK (AP) — Siân Heder's follow-up to the best picture-winning “CODA” chronicles the disability rights pioneer Judy Heumann. Heumann died at the age of 75 in 2023 while Heder was developing the movie with her. She resolved to push on with the project to honor Heumann and try to bring some of her accessibility gains to the movie industry. Characters with disabilities remain extremely uncommon in Hollywood productions, and big-screen biopics like “Being Heumann” are even more seldom. “Being Heumann,” starring Ruth Madeley as Heumann, features the largest ensemble ever of performers with disabilities. Oscar-winning Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio dies at 52 SANTIAGO, Chile (AP) — Oscar-winning Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio has died in Santiago, Chile, at 52. His family announced his death Friday on Instagram, citing health reasons but not specifying the cause. Lelio was known for his groundbreaking film “A Fantastic Woman,” which portrayed a transgender woman and won the Academy Award for best international film. It was Chile's second Oscar win. Lelio’s other works include "Gloria," "The Wonder," and “Disobedience.” He had begun filming “Poeta Chileno” in September. Born in Argentina, Lelio moved to Chile at age two and studied at the Chilean Film School. ... 'ER' and 'The Pitt' are similar enough for lawsuit to move forward, appeals court finds LOS ANGELES (AP) — A California appeals court has found enough similarity between “ER” and “The Pitt” for a lawsuit by Michael Crichton's widow to proceed. The court ruled that the trial judge was correct to reject Warner Bros. Television's motion to dismiss. Both shows star Noah Wyle as an emergency room doctor and focus on the healthcare system. The lawsuit argues “The Pitt” is an unauthorized “ER” reboot. Crichton had a contract preventing any “ER” spinoffs without his consent. The court dismissed claims against Wyle and others, finding no evidence they interfered with Crichton's contract.
